item.title: Carney Calls for E.U.-Canada Pact Amid ‘Ferocious Storm’
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney told European lawmakers that an alliance would help to secure sovereignty and independence for his country. The moves come amid a historic low for U.S. ties with Canada.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada addressing the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, on Thursday.

item.title: Mexico City Has a Toxic ‘Sacrifice Zone’ Where Cancer Is Surging
item.description: For decades, the Mexican authorities have sacrificed a rural valley to flush away the capital’s waste and power the economy. Now, local communities are paying for that decision — often with peoples’ lives.
item.dc:creator: Emiliano Rodríguez Mega and Alejandro Cegarra
item.media:credit: Alejandro Cegarra for The New York Times
item.media:description: The old church of San Francisco Bojay in Hidalgo, Mexico, is partially submerged after the area was flooded in 1949 to create the Endhó Dam.

item.title: Trump Sanctions on Cuba Strands Thousands Of Shipping Containers
item.description: The U.S. says its sanctions are not aimed at depriving Cuba of essential goods. Thousands of stranded shipping containers tell a different story.
item.dc:creator: Ed Augustin and Frances Robles
item.media:description: Ships unloading humanitarian aid at the Port of Havana this year. The challenges in shipping to the island nation are intensifying a humanitarian crisis.

item.title: A New Play in Budapest Signals a Cultural Reawakening for Hungary
item.description: A one-woman show about the perils of authoritarianism draws on a memoir by the Hungarian-American writer Kati Marton. Under Viktor Orban’s government, it might not have happened.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Higgins
item.media:credit: Akos Stiller for The New York Times
item.media:description: The August premiere in Budapest of the one-woman play “Enemies of the People,” starring the Hungarian film and stage actress Erika Marozsan.

item.title: The Hidden Human Cost of Kim Jong-un’s New Power

item.dc:creator: Choe Sang-Hun
item.media:credit: Kim Won Jin/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: North Korea celebrated the 78th anniversary of its founding with a parade last week in Pyongyang, the capital. The country is now in one of the strongest positions it has ever been in, financially and diplomatically.

item.title: At Least 21 Dead in Gaza After Building Collapse, Officials Say

item.title: After a Desperate Search for Survivors, Rescuers Find Bodies at Nepal Power Plant

item.title: Man Suspected of Pushing Woman in Front of London Bus Is Found Dead, British News Media Say

item.title: State Department Extends Visa Ban on Abbas, Other Palestinian Officials
